mutants.reason: With the default parameters (ASSERT > RELEASE), a release attempt clears the counter at RELEASE_CLKS-1 and never reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Once flag_out is high, it never goes low again, even when flag_in stays low indefinitely.

mutants.description: The restart on agreement is applied only when flag_in is high, so an aborted assert attempt (flag_in back low while flag_out is low) leaves its partial count in place
mutants.reason: While flag_out is low, short high glitches on flag_in now add up across gaps instead of each restarting from zero. flag_out asserts once the glitches total ASSERT_CLKS clocks, even though no single pulse was that long: a false fault from switching-node pickup.

mutants.description: target_clks is written as a terminal count (qualification time minus one), while both compares still subtract one again, so every transition qualifies one clock early
mutants.reason: In both directions, flag_out now follows a steady new level of flag_in after ASSERT_CLKS-1 or RELEASE_CLKS-1 clocks of disagreement instead of ASSERT_CLKS or RELEASE_CLKS. The edge reaches the supervisor one clock early.

mutants.description: The clear-on-qualify restart only happens when a release qualifies; on the edge an assert qualifies the disagreement count is left at ASSERT_CLKS-1
mutants.reason: Suppose an assert qualifies and flag_in drops on the very next clock. The leftover count is already at or past RELEASE_CLKS-1, so flag_out releases after one low clock instead of RELEASE_CLKS clocks.

mutants.description: The flag_out flip compares the disagreement count against the release time for both directions, so the longer assert qualification is forgotten
mutants.reason: When flag_in goes high and stays high while flag_out is low, flag_out asserts after RELEASE_CLKS clocks (200 us) instead of ASSERT_CLKS (1 ms). An assert-going pulse between those two lengths now gets through.

mutants.description: The counter's clear-on-qualify limit is hard-coded to the release time, so during an assert attempt the count restarts every RELEASE_CLKS clocks and never reaches the assert target
mutants.reason: Once flag_out has released, a flag_in that holds high for any length of time never makes flag_out assert again, because the count is cleared at RELEASE_CLKS-1 before it reaches ASSERT_CLKS-1. Releases still qualify normally.

mutants.description: The flip rule is written for the assert direction only (flag_in high while flag_out low), so a qualified release never updates flag_out
mutants.reason: With RESET_VALUE=1, flag_out comes out of reset high and stays high however long flag_in holds low. The supervisor therefore never sees the fault clear.

mutants.description: The restart on agreement is applied only when flag_in is low, so an aborted release attempt (flag_in dips low while flag_out is high, then returns high) leaves its partial count in the disagreement counter
mutants.reason: With flag_out high, a low glitch on flag_in shorter than RELEASE_CLKS leaves the counter at the glitch length. A later low pulse then releases flag_out early, once the two together reach RELEASE_CLKS, instead of after RELEASE_CLKS continuous low clocks. Aborted asserts are still restarted correctly.

mutants.description: The flip compare adds a one-clock lookahead (counter+1) to make up for flag_out being registered, so flag_out flips one clock before the counter reaches its target and restarts
mutants.reason: Every transition with a target of 2 or more clocks shows up at flag_out one clock early. Because the counter only restarts on the next edge, an immediate reversal after an assert starts with the counter at ASSERT_CLKS-1, which is already past the release target, so flag_out flips straight back after one clock instead of waiting RELEASE_CLKS.

mutants.description: The disagreement counter measures flag_in against the fail-safe reset level RESET_VALUE instead of the believed state flag_out, so it counts time away from reset rather than time disagreeing with flag_out
mutants.reason: With the default RESET_VALUE=1, a low flag_in still qualifies and releases flag_out after RELEASE_CLKS. After that, a high flag_in clears the counter every clock instead of counting, so a real fault that holds flag_in high for any length of time never re-asserts flag_out.

mutants.description: The release qualification time is written as a terminal count (RELEASE_CLKS-1), but the assert time is not, so only a release qualifies one clock early
mutants.reason: After flag_in goes low and stays low while flag_out is high, flag_out falls after RELEASE_CLKS-1 clocks instead of RELEASE_CLKS. The assert timing does not change.

mutants.description: The disagreement counter only counts the release direction (flag_in low while flag_out is high), the move away from the high reset state, so an assert attempt never builds a count
mutants.reason: Once flag_out has released, flag_in going high and staying high leaves the counter at 0. The flip compare against ASSERT_CLKS-1 never passes, so flag_out never re-asserts.

mutants.description: The disagreement counter is preloaded to a full count in reset, so the first input level seen after reset is accepted without debouncing
mutants.reason: With flag_in low when rst_n is released, flag_out (reset high) falls on the first clock instead of after RELEASE_CLKS clocks of stable low. A glitch at that moment is passed straight through.

mutants.description: The disagreement counter only counts an assert attempt (flag_in high while flag_out is low), so the release direction never builds a count
mutants.reason: With the default fail-safe RESET_VALUE of 1, flag_out comes out of reset high and a healthy (low) flag_in never builds a count, so flag_out stays asserted forever and the supervisor never sees the fault clear.

mutants.description: flag_out is only allowed to flip when flag_in moves away from the fail-safe RESET_VALUE, so a return to the reset level (a re-asserted fault, with the default RESET_VALUE of 1) never updates flag_out
mutants.reason: After the first qualified release, flag_out is low. A real fault that holds flag_in high for ASSERT_CLKS clocks or more lets the counter reach its target and restart, but flag_out never asserts again.

withdrawn.description: The disagreement counter's clear-on-qualify limit uses CNT_MAX instead of the selected target, so the count is not restarted on the edge a release qualifies
withdrawn.reason: When flag_out releases and flag_in goes high again on the very next clock, the counter keeps counting up from RELEASE_CLKS. flag_out then asserts after only ASSERT_CLKS-RELEASE_CLKS clocks of high input instead of ASSERT_CLKS.
